Six builds across three ideas: agents should run repeatable processes, LLMs should work with meaning rather than templates, and markets should be understood as networks.

Six systems

What they do.

6 shown

01 / Agent-led systems

FinX Intelligence Agent

Reads a defined set of market voices and turns their ticker talk into a weekly brief, so research can see what the crowd is arguing about instead of scrolling a feed.

  • A scheduled job pulls posts from a chosen account list.
  • Each ticker mention is scored for sentiment, conviction and a short rationale.
  • Those scores become weekly metrics: volume, movers, new tickers and disagreement.
  • The run writes a static dashboard and an email summary.

01 / Agent-led systems

OutboundOS

Runs outbound as a scheduled workflow that cannot act until a person approves it, so go-to-market stays repeatable without turning into unsupervised automation.

  • A campaign brief becomes a scheduled research task.
  • The run writes a proposal. It does not send or publish anything.
  • A person approves or rejects that proposal.
  • Only an approval can produce the output, and every step is kept in a log.
Repository ↗

01 / Agent-led systems

AI Agent Traffic Listener

Measures which AI agents visit a website and ignores ordinary human browsing, so marketing can see a new discovery channel without collecting a second set of personal data.

  • It sits on the server, in the path of incoming requests.
  • A registry labels known agents. Unfamiliar bot-shaped traffic is kept aside for review.
  • Normal browser visits are dropped.
  • Stored events have no IP address and no query string, and are written after the response.
  • A report groups visits by agent, vendor, purpose and page.
Repository ↗

02 / Semantic intelligence

Campaign Resonance Engine

Finds companies whose own language already matches a campaign idea, so targeting is based on what they say rather than on firmographics alone.

  • A campaign is written as a set of phrases to look for.
  • Those phrases are searched across passages from company sites.
  • Every hit keeps the passage, the score and the source URL.
  • Companies rank by how many of the phrases they match, not by one lucky hit.
Repository ↗

02 / Semantic intelligence

Semantic Market Profiler

Turns an open market question into evidence-backed company profiles, so research can qualify a market that does not exist as a bought database field.

  • A person writes the question, the sources and the signals to look for.
  • Nothing is processed until that plan is explicitly approved.
  • Each match keeps the exact passage it came from.
  • Companies are then qualified against rules the operator can edit.
Repository ↗

03 / Network analysis

GraphGTM

Maps a market as people, communities and bridges, then suggests who to approach, so go-to-market starts from relationships instead of a flat account list.

  • People and the ties between them become a graph.
  • PageRank, betweenness and Louvain communities show influence, bridges and clusters.
  • Search looks for a concept and keeps the passage that caused the match.
  • Suggested entry points combine that match with where the person sits in the network.
